summary_en: This phase 2 study compares two ways of giving chemotherapy after surgery and HIPEC for malignant peritoneal mesothelioma: directly into the abdomen (intraperitoneal) or into a vein (intravenous). The drugs are pemetrexed plus cisplatin or carboplatin; the intravenous arm gives 4 cycles, with up to 6 at clinician discretion, and the number of intraperitoneal cycles is not stated. The main outcome measure is not stated in the record; the study is a randomized phase 2 trial.
summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 compara dos formas de administrar quimioterapia después de la cirugía y la HIPEC para el mesotelioma peritoneal maligno: directamente en el abdomen (intraperitoneal) o en una vena (intravenosa). Los medicamentos son pemetrexed más cisplatino o carboplatino; el brazo intravenoso recibe 4 ciclos, con hasta 6 a criterio del médico, y el número de ciclos intraperitoneales no se indica. El resultado principal que se mide no se indica en el registro; el estudio es un ensayo aleatorizado de fase 2.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with a clinical diagnosis of malignant peritoneal mesothelioma
Epithelioid histology confirmed by pathology before randomization
Complete or near-complete cytoreductive surgery achieved or planned
ECOG performance status of 1 or less
Adequate blood counts, kidney function and liver function, and agreement to use contraception
not_for: Prior intraperitoneal or systemic chemotherapy or immunotherapy for peritoneal mesothelioma
Biopsy showing sarcomatoid, well-differentiated papillary or benign multicystic mesothelioma
Other prior cancers, with some exceptions, unless no activity for more than three years
Known allergy to cisplatin, carboplatin, pemetrexed or mitomycin
